body:
Fusion rewrites and escapes the same requirement keys for every entity while constructing lookup variable sets.

The one-, two-, and three-requirement fast paths now reuse encoded keys for multi-item batches. Keys are cached weakly by the compiled requirement and encoded on the first valid use. Each batch resolves a key once and reuses its bytes for the remaining entities. Single-item batches keep the existing string-writing path. Cold cache fills allocate a byte array per used requirement; warm per-call allocations are unchanged.

### Benchmarks

The direct benchmark calls `FetchResultStore.CreateVariableValueSets` with compiled operations and completed result data. Plan compilation, source JSON parsing, result completion, initialization, and cleanup are outside the timed region. Results below are medians of eight samples of 5,000 calls, after a two-second warmup per case, using Release assemblies on .NET 10.0.12 ARM64, pinned to one CPU with tiered compilation disabled. `main` is `f58f46db8e`; the PR is `cd16f0324f`.

#### Single requirement

| Entities | Version | Median | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | `main` | 222.1 ns | 1.00 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| 1 | PR | 227.7 ns | 1.03 | 64 B | 1.00 |
| 3 | `main` | 468.7 ns | 1.00 | 144 B | 1.00 |
| 3 | PR | 436.3 ns | 0.93 | 144 B | 1.00 |
| 20 | `main` | 2,448.7 ns | 1.00 | 824 B | 1.00 |
| 20 | PR | 2,208.4 ns | 0.90 | 824 B | 1.00 |

The single-entity PR samples had 9.2% coefficient of variation, and the three-entity baseline had 20.8%. These small differences need more evidence. The 20-entity samples had at most 1.1% variation.

#### Three requirements, 20 entities

The duplicate case contains three distinct variable sets. The sparse case has a valid required ID on only three entities.

| Case | Version | Median | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Distinct | `main` | 4,959.6 ns | 1.00 | 824 B | 1.00 |
| Distinct | PR | 4,125.7 ns | 0.83 | 824 B | 1.00 |
| Duplicates | `main` | 4,942.9 ns | 1.00 | 304 B | 1.00 |
| Duplicates | PR | 4,161.6 ns | 0.84 | 304 B | 1.00 |
| Sparse | `main` | 1,208.1 ns | 1.00 | 144 B | 1.00 |
| Sparse | PR | 1,088.2 ns | 0.90 | 144 B | 1.00 |

#### Fallback paths, 20 entities

These cases exercise the general path, whose key-writing strategy is unchanged.

| Case | Version | Median | Ratio | Allocated | Alloc Ratio |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Four requirements | `main` | 13,044.4 ns | 1.00 | 824 B | 1.00 |
| Four requirements | PR | 12,859.2 ns | 0.99 | 824 B | 1.00 |
| Three requirements plus a forwarded variable | `main` | 6,863.4 ns | 1.00 | 824 B | 1.00 |
| Three requirements plus a forwarded variable | PR | 6,828.1 ns | 0.99 | 824 B | 1.00 |

#### HTTP requests

The gateway measurements use 16 virtual users, a 20-second warmup, three 20-second measured runs, four subgraphs with 4 ms simulated latency, and default production tiering. Responses were validated against the saved reference bodies. Values are medians across runs; CPU is gateway process CPU time per completed request.

The existing baseline runs were reused and were not interleaved with this candidate. These comparisons show higher CPU per request and lower throughput; the direct-method gains do not establish an end-to-end improvement.

| Query shape | Response | Version | Requests/s | Gateway CPU/request |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 20 product lookups | 1,786 B | `main` | 1,041.8 | 0.3029 ms |
| 20 product lookups | 1,786 B | PR | 990.3 (-4.9%) | 0.3224 ms (+6.5%) |
| 3 products with reviews and authors | 3,382 B | `main` | 770.7 | 0.4156 ms |
| 3 products with reviews and authors | 3,382 B | PR | 718.0 (-6.8%) | 0.4602 ms (+10.7%) |

### Validation

- Release build: zero warnings or errors.
- Focused unit tests: 73 passed.
- Integration tests: 155 passed, three existing skips.
- Two review passes completed without outstanding findings.
